The presence of Slc29a1 in the pathway implies that it may play a role in regulating the activity of Slc29a2, possibly through direct interaction or by influencing the cellular environment in which the transporter operates. The integration of these pathways suggests that Zalcitabine could interfere with the function of the nucleoside transporter, potentially affecting nucleoside transport and leading to cellular dysfunction.
